# Food Profile Template

> For a food that is part of ordinary Nigerian eating — not a supplement and not
> a branded product.
>
> **The rule that overrides everything else in this template:** never describe a
> food as curing, treating, healing or preventing a condition. A food profile
> describes what a food *contains*, what people *use it for*, and how to *eat it
> safely*. If you cannot support a health claim with a proper source, leave it
> out. Describing food as medicine is not an exaggeration NHECOF will publish.

---

## 4. Key nutrients

> Add one row per nutrient. Write "Amount / Value" in a form a normal reader
> understands. If you are quoting a number, it must come from a source, and you
> must say which part of the food and whether the value is raw or cooked.

| Nutrient | Amount / Value | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| | | |
| | | |
| | | |

**Source for these values:** _______________________

**Raw, cooked, or as normally eaten?** _______________

> If a value varies a lot by variety, soil or preparation, say so here. "Values
> vary widely depending on variety and preparation" is more honest than a single
> number that happens to be right for one bag of leaves.

---

## 5. Potential benefits

> **Evidence-supported only.** Write these as possibilities, not promises.
>
> Instead of "prevents high blood pressure", write "is part of a diet
> associated with lower blood pressure" — and cite the source.

_______________________________________________

_______________________________________________

_______________________________________________

- [ ] Every benefit here has a reference at the bottom of this profile
- [ ] No benefit is written as a guarantee
- [ ] Nothing here suggests the food replaces medicine or a visit to a clinic

## 8. Cautions

> **This field is required by the Studio.** If there genuinely are no known
> cautions, type `None known` — do not leave it blank.
>
> Always consider: allergies, conditions where the food needs limiting,
> interactions with medication, and whether the food is unsafe raw.

| Check | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| Any known allergy or intolerance | |
| Diabetes / blood sugar considerations | |
| Blood pressure or kidney considerations | |
| Pregnancy considerations | |
| Children considerations | |
| Interaction with medication or supplements | |
| Must it be cooked? | |
| Spoilage, and how to tell it has gone off | |
| Any part that should not be eaten | |

**Overall caution note:** _______________________________________

- [ ] I have not told a reader to use this food in place of prescribed medicine
- [ ] I have told readers which group should ask a professional first

## 10. Affordable meal ideas

> Three or four ways to eat it that a family can afford. Name the dish. Use
> foods that are cheap and widely available. These should be meals, not garnish
> suggestions.

1. **Dish:** ______________ **Ingredients:** ______________ **Roughly:** ______________
2. **Dish:** ______________ **Ingredients:** ______________ **Roughly:** ______________
3. **Dish:** ______________ **Ingredients:** ______________ **Roughly:** ______________
4. **Dish:** ______________ **Ingredients:** ______________ **Roughly:** ______________

> If you cannot say what a dish costs without guessing, write "cost varies" and
> do not put a number on it. Never invent prices.

## 13. Final check

- [ ] I have not used cure, treat, heal, prevent or guarantee about this food
- [ ] Cautions field filled in, even if it says "None known"
- [ ] Every nutrient value has a source and says raw or cooked
- [ ] Benefits are written as possibilities with sources
- [ ] Portion context uses Nigerian household measures
- [ ] At least three affordable, named meal ideas
- [ ] No invented prices
- [ ] Nothing here replaces medical advice
- [ ] Image consent recorded, or no image used
- [ ] Review Status set to **Submitted for Review**
- [ ] Reviewer has actually been told
